facts.statement: The study addresses radiation-induced brain injury, a complication that occurs in up to 30% of patients who receive cranial radiotherapy.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers used a mouse model where animals received 6 gray of whole-body irradiation to test the treatment.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study design involved combining the new nanomaterial with live electrical recording of brain activity to measure changes in neural function.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks successfully restored the electrical firing patterns of medium spiny neurons and the activity of striatal brain circuits.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Treatment with the nanonetworks led to improvements in the mice's movement and anxiety-related behaviors.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The treatment ensured that all treated mice survived for 30 days, protected sensitive organs from radiation damage, and helped blood cell production recover.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors suggest that neuronal excitability is a previously underexplored target for treating radiation-induced brain injury.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors note that previous research has been limited because drugs struggle to cross the blood-brain barrier and existing methods cannot track dynamic changes in brain function.
facts.subject: humans
